objective: Review Filamajig NFC M3 portable spool identity and label implementation for offline interoperability, versioning, profile/spool identity integrity, import/export fidelity, Unicode/QR behavior, Android lifecycle and UI, persistence transactions, collision recovery, privacy, and documentation accuracy.
owner_requirements: Provide a working prototype of portable local filament/spool identity without requiring a server or account
Generate a self-contained QR and a full export/import bundle, preserving provenance on the full bundle
Keep reusable filament profile identity separate from each owned physical spool identity
Support configurable human-readable label output including temperatures, identifiers, and transmission distance
Operate offline on the Motorola Razr 2023 and preserve existing local records and NFC behavior
change_summary: Added deterministic filamajig.spool version 1 UTF-8 JSON encoding with compact QR and source-bearing bundle forms
Added strict decode results for supported, future-version preserved bytes, and rejected inputs with 64 KiB decode and 2,048-byte QR limits
Added local camera QR bypass of AI, pasted-bundle review import, configurable portable label dialog, and explicit Android sharing

Persisted imported profile/spool IDs and quantities transactionally, supports multiple spools sharing a profile, rejects spool/reassignment collisions atomically, and deletes shared/final profiles correctly
Corrected strict JSON parsing for valid escaped and literal surrogate pairs while retaining rejection of unpaired surrogates
Added host and real-device acceptance plus architecture, schema, offline recovery, privacy, and roadmap documentation

objective_evidence.host: Protected full gate PASS before final small error-reporting refinement: 97 tasks for core tests, app unit/storage tests, lint, app APK and Android-test APK. Focused tests PASS after persistence/parser remediation. Evidence command will rebuild current source.
objective_evidence.device: Installed APK and Android-test APK only on verified motorola razr 2023. DevicePortableIdentityAcceptanceTest PASS in 4.186 seconds through actual JPEG QR decode path; 575-byte payload, exact Prismático 雪 Unicode, distinct IDs, remaining quantity, network_required false. Visible UI confirms home import button and a real local-spool dialog with 609-byte QR, controls, distinct IDs, and share action.

known_limits: Version 1 imports filament fields, profile/spool IDs, and quantities; broader purchase, vendor, location, notes, tag bindings, and custom spool metadata are outside the M3 format
Compact QR omits per-field source strings to control capacity; the separately shared full bundle retains those sources
The UI offers Android text sharing rather than managing a filesystem document internally
The real-device acceptance programmatically exercises the production decoder and separately inspects visible surfaces; it does not photographically scan a printed label during this cycle
review_questions: Is any architecture, data-loss, collision, security/privacy, versioning, encoding, Android lifecycle, accessibility, or interoperability defect release-blocking for M3?

Do the tests prove offline deterministic round trip, forward-version handling, Unicode, capacity, shared-profile persistence, atomic collision rollback, delete behavior, and real-device decoder execution?
Does the schema and documentation make app-removal survivability and the distinction between profile and physical-spool identity precise?
sanitization: No credentials, environment values, user database contents, NFC UIDs, device serials, network addresses, photos, or account data are included.
